references.text: Moses calls the people of Israel a 'crooked and twisted generation', which mirrors Jesus' words about a 'faithless and twisted generation'.
Moses describes the people of Israel as corrupt and not his children, similar to Jesus' description of that generation as 'faithless and twisted'.
The psalm mentions a generation that was unfaithful to God, parallel to Jesus' description of his own generation.
God expresses frustration over the rebellious people of Israel, just as Jesus expressed frustration over the faithless and twisted generation.
Jesus refers to the generation as 'an evil and adulterous generation', which aligns with his statement in Matthew 17:17.
Here too the generation is called 'an evil and adulterous generation', repeating the theme from Matthew 17:17.
Jesus expresses frustration over the disciples' lack of understanding, similar to his expression of frustration in Matthew 17:17.
